newsitem.title: USA: US Plains cattle trade moderate at $64 - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: US Plains cattle trade moderate at $64 - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle near midday sold at $64.00 per cwt in moderate trade, unchanged from Wednesday, feedlot sources said.
About 11,000 head had sold in the Texas Panhandle and western Oklahoma area and about 10,000 in Kansas, they said.
"It started last night and we pretty well tipped it over at $64.00, there's no chance of getting anything better this week," a Kansas feedlot operator said.
Onwers had expected $65.00 prices for cattle as beef prices jumped this week, but in the end, sold at $64.00 amid ideas beef demand was slowing, several cattle feeders said.
Beef prices this week rose quickly amid moderate retail demand for Independence Day advertising features, with gains accelerated by fairly tight beef stocks, sources said.

Choice beef weighing 700-850 lbs at midday Thursday was quoted at $103.77 per cwt, up $5.65 since Friday, USDA statistics showed. Beef prices at midday were quoted up $0.02 to $0.44, with heavyweight choice up $0.04 at $103.77, USDA reported.
Once packers finish buying cattle to supply retailers with beef for holiday promotions, beef demand was seen slowing, which could drag fed cattle prices lower, sources said.
